title: Shortest paths
learn: Dijkstra (heap), Bellman-Ford (negative edges, k-edge limit), when BFS is enough. A* concept only
hook: Network Delay Time is the textbook Dijkstra question, and Cheapest Flights Within K Stops is the classic twist that breaks plain Dijkstra. Knowing which shortest-path algorithm fits which constraint is a strong interview signal.

explain.prompt: Explain Dijkstra's algorithm, why it needs non-negative weights, and its complexity with a heap.
keyPoints: keep the best known distance to every node; start with the source at 0
repeatedly pop the unsettled node with the smallest distance from a min-heap and relax its edges
with non-negative weights, the popped node's distance can't improve later, so it's final
O((V + E) log V) with a heap; skip stale heap entries
negative weights or an edge-count limit → Bellman-Ford; unweighted → plain BFS
